title: Harvard Blaschka receiving craft actor crosswalk, 1892–1932
research_question: How were the material, legal and administrative operations required to receive and install the Glass Flowers distributed among actors inside and outside Harvard?

operations: authorize transition out of customs-controlled state

actor_rows.institutional_position: museum assistant/technical collections worker; later Assistant and Technician / Curator of Botanical Collections
actor_rows.later_control: Harvard Crimson obituary says joined museum 1901, early duty unpacking crates; official HOLLIS preserves Bierweiler papers/1931 diary

boundary_changes.configuration: receiving depends heavily on curator + patron + porter + broker/customs; technical labor is visible but only partly named
Waugh appears explicitly as paid external pack/setup/unpack contractor with independent workshop; Ware remains skilled unpacker; customs-supervised unpacking is staged publicly
museum begins explicitly describing preservation/installation skill as staff competence; Bierweiler is salaried and making/wiring plaques while Waugh remains a separate craft resource
Harvard reports publicly/administratively on Bierweiler's long training, handling skill, mounting technique and museum traditions; Waugh simultaneously continues building cases
Bierweiler spans clearing, support removal, repair, remounting and unpacking; Rudolf directly recognizes him as the receiver-side skilled counterpart

interpretive_model.not_a_linear_professionalization_story: The evidence does not show a clean transition from amateur to professional or contractor to registrar. Patron, curator, contractor and museum assistant remain concurrent.
interpretive_model.stronger_model: A mixed receiving ecology progressively made distinct forms of expertise visible and durable. Some capacity remained outsourced to a local workshop; some became embodied in long-serving museum staff; some remained attached to patronage or curatorial office.
interpretive_model.transport_implication: The route ends only when this receiving ecology has successfully undone the transport assemblage and rebuilt a stable museum object.

map_implication: Keep these actors in Harvard-node state/authority timeline rather than drawing separate geographical routes. Waugh's 113 Mt. Auburn workshop could eventually appear as a local inset only if a Cambridge-scale map becomes useful.
